assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy link basic gut-hormone biology to a transformative treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large, lasting clinical and societal impact and a clear originating discovery chain.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and GLP-1 secretion and action), Drucker (proglucagon-derived peptide biology and therapeutic concept) and Knudsen (translation into a long-acting analogue) form a coherent trio; Mojsov's sequence and structural work is a real credit question the three-person limit leaves open.
assessment.maturity: Efficacy is confirmed by many independent large trials, including cardiovascular and renal outcomes, and the field is mature; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Mojsov's role versus the other contributors is disputed and may be unresolved.
Whether the committee prefers to recognise the physiology or the drug-development contribution (Knudsen) is a judgment call.
I rely on my own knowledge of the history and have not verified details independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells represent a new therapeutic modality that produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, with major clinical impact and strong conceptual originality in cell therapy.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CAR design and costimulation), June (clinical translation, first durable CLL responses) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early clinical CAR/TIL work) are a plausible trio; Eshhar and others with early CAR design are not in the supplied credit, so the configuration is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and a decade of follow-up confirm the benefit, though long-term toxicity, access and solid-tumour limits remain; timely.
uncertainties: Supplied credit omits early CAR pioneers, weakening a fair allocation.
Durability beyond several years and secondary malignancy risk are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a central driver of chronic inflammation and that its blockade controls rheumatoid arthritis changed the treatment of RA, IBD and other immune-mediated diseases, a clear bench-to-bedside paradigm. As a rheumatology physician-scientist I know the clinical impact first-hand but weigh it by the common criteria.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini made the decisive mechanistic and clinical proof-of-concept contributions; the two-person credit is clean, though antibody engineering and others contributed to the products.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent clinical confirmation and a widely accepted mechanism; very mature, with recognition arguably long awaited.
uncertainties: Others (for example antibody and TNF-biology pioneers) may be argued to share credit.
Prior Lasker recognition does not by itself settle Nobel merit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific control with light, transforming circuit research across fields; originality and lasting methodological impact are very high, though direct therapeutic impact is still emerging.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and its implementation in neurons (Deisseroth, Boyden, Miesenböck's earlier concept) make credit highly contested; a three-person limit forces exclusion of at least three credited people.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated for over fifteen years and a standard tool; the first clinical vision-restoration applications are early.
uncertainties: Allocation among six credited people is the main obstacle.
Whether a methods discovery will be judged as having conferred the greatest benefit to humankind.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response defined a fundamental intracellular signalling pathway between ER and nucleus, explains proteostasis in disease and has been therapeutically relevant, with strong originality and clarity.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori made the decisive contributions (Ire1/Hac1 pathway, UPR transcription); a clean two-person credit, though Ron Davis-era and Kozutsumi's early work, and mammalian UPR contributors, are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Broadly confirmed across yeast and mammals over three decades; mature, though therapeutic translation is still modest.
uncertainties: Other contributors to the early UPR and mammalian pathways may need credit.
Clinical impact is more indirect than for therapy-based candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: VLP-based HPV vaccines prevent infection and cervical and other cancers, with large demonstrated population-level declines in disease; the impact is exceptional and the work is original and clear, and the surrounding area has been recognised with the 2008 prize for HPV discovery.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP formation and immunogenicity) and Frazer (vaccine development) are the commonly cited trio; Zhou and others also contributed to VLP work, so credit is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Population-level effectiveness data over more than a decade are strong; timing is mature.
uncertainties: Attribution among Frazer, Zhou, Lowy, Schiller and others is disputed.
Possible committee reluctance given the earlier HPV-related prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defined the cytosolic DNA-sensing pathway of innate immunity, with relevance to infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer; high originality and broad conceptual influence, with translation still developing.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAS and cGAMP identification) and Barber (STING) are the key figures; other STING discoverers (e.g. Ishikawa) and cGAS-related contributors complicate credit.
assessment.maturity: Replicated extensively, but clinical agents are still in early trials; somewhat early for prize recognition.
uncertainties: Allocation among several near-simultaneous STING discoveries is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids created a widely used experimental system for tissue biology, disease modelling and personalised medicine, building on Lgr5 stem-cell work; originality and uptake are high.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the conceptual and technical advance and Sato made the key early organoid demonstration; credit is reasonably clean, though other organoid and stem-cell pioneers could be argued for.
assessment.maturity: The method is replicated worldwide; clinical and regenerative applications are still emerging, so maturity is moderate.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers recognising the underlying Lgr5 stem-cell discovery over the organoid method.
Clinical impact is not yet established.
